analysis.title: "Almost A Down Round": OpenAI Slashes Funding Target By $10 Billion As AI Rout Spoils "Last Chance" Pitch
key_insights: Per the FT (Oct 31), OpenAI cut its private funding round target to about $20B at a $1.25T valuation, from a $30B raise at $1.4T pitched in early October. The commitment deadline was Oct 31, and the first close is expected to bring in less than $20B after some investors lowered their allocations.

The round's largest participant is expected to be a UAE consortium including MGX, with OpenAI getting an option to lease newly developed computing power in the region. Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz and SoftBank also plan to participate.

A later retail offering to wealthy individuals at $1.25T 'could expand the round to $20bn or so', so the headline figure depends on the wealthy-client channel that Morgan Stanley's clients met with 'a bit of a thud' a week earlier.

The author's math (approximate): $20B at $1.25T buys about 1.6% of OpenAI, against about 14% in March, when OpenAI raised a record $122B at $852B. $1.25T is still a 47% markup to March. It is an 11% markdown to the $1.4T price OpenAI put on the table a month earlier.

OpenAI told investors on Oct 8 that its revenue run rate was approaching $50B, about $20B below figures that had been circulating. At $1.25T the company trades at about 25x that run rate. It has about $1.5T of compute commitments.
The FT names Anthropic's upcoming IPO (next month, at '$1.5tn or more') as a reason investors are waiting. OpenAI's private valuation now sits below what Anthropic is expected to fetch in public.

Some of Anthropic's own investors marked its valuation down to $1.5T from $2T earlier in October. The FT reported on Oct 31 that Blackstone told Anthropic it may not get an investment-grade rating after the IPO and is expected to land a 'high' junk rating.

Goldman credit strategists (Amanda Lynam, Global Credit Trader) expect 'BBs to absorb the brunt of future AI-related financing'. Goldman's Gabriela Borges argues the AI funding gap may be smaller than feared, citing vendor prepayments, BYO-hardware, installed-base cash generation, $19T of private markets ($4.5T of capacity to deploy per Preqin) and Nvidia's $500B financing pool.

The Goldman note concedes room for 'another $500bn of IG issuance' from hyperscalers while warning that AI-related gross debt extends well beyond the hyperscaler universe. Microsoft drew $115B of demand for a jumbo bond deal (Bloomberg, via JPM Market Intel), while OpenAI could not fill a $30B equity round.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky (Oct 30 and the prior week) said core businesses funding the AI buildout face greater scrutiny, citing Amazon's first ad miss in seven quarters and trailing FCF of negative $42B. He said the assumption of unlimited cheap capital is being challenged: cut capex, delay deployment or fund through equity.

On Friday (Oct 30) the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% and briefly entered correction territory, Intel had its biggest drop on record, and Nasdaq 100 members had erased more than $1.2T of market cap in October before the open.
Goldman's Tony Pasquariello: the bank's momentum basket has logged 39 one-day moves above 5% in 2026, the most since at least 1999 except 2020 (42) and ahead of 2000 (32). 27 of the 39 were selloffs.

JPM's Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou found retail put record amounts into leveraged ETFs recently to buy the AI dip. Nomura's Charlie McElligott warned of a $35B levered ETF dump into the close. Barclays is publishing guides on shorting AI-linked credit via CDS.
JPM's Andrew Tyler remains 'Tactically Bullish' but says the AI trade 'remains crowded with exceptionally high sentiment bars to clear'.

The author's view is that OpenAI's next round likely prices off Anthropic's post-IPO trading level. The bull case is a strong Anthropic pricing in November and an AI stock bounce into year-end, which most of Goldman's credit clients see as likeliest although 'few have positions on for this move'.

sector_views.rationale: The author is skeptical on AI funding. Private round sizes and valuations are shrinking, momentum is volatile, retail leverage is high, and AI-related debt is expected to be rated BB.

earnings_insights: Amazon posted its first advertising miss in seven quarters, with trailing free cash flow of negative $42B (per Goldman's Privorotsky, Oct 30). The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
Intel had its biggest one-day drop on record on Friday Oct 30. The report gives no earnings figures.
risk_factors: OpenAI's remaining funding need is about $1.5T of compute commitments, so it will need to return to capital markets before an IPO that is at least a year away.
Anthropic's IPO may price poorly or carry a high-junk rating, which could reset private AI valuations.
A $35B levered ETF unwind and record retail leveraged ETF positioning could amplify selloffs.
Wealthy-client demand for OpenAI shares at $1.25T may be weak, putting the round's $20B headline at risk.
AI-related gross debt extends beyond the hyperscalers, and BB-rated issuers are expected to absorb the brunt of financing.
vol_and_positioning: The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% on Oct 30 and briefly entered correction territory.
Goldman's momentum basket has logged 39 one-day moves above 5% in 2026, 27 of them selloffs.
Retail put record amounts into leveraged ETFs to buy the AI dip. Nomura's McElligott flagged a $35B levered ETF dump into the close.
The AI CDS market is described as the hottest trade on Wall Street, and Barclays has published guides on shorting it.
JPM's Tyler describes the AI trade as crowded with exceptionally high sentiment bars to clear.
geopolitical: UAE state-backed investment groups, including MGX, are expected to be the largest participants in OpenAI's round, which includes an option for OpenAI to lease computing power in the region.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Borges argues the funding gap is smaller than feared, while Goldman's credit strategists see room for another $500bn of IG issuance and expect BBs to absorb the brunt of AI financing.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Borges argues the funding gap is smaller than feared, citing vendor prepayments, installed-base cash flow, $4.5T of private dry powder and Nvidia's $500bn financing pool. Goldman credit clients see an AI bounce into year-end as likeliest.
tension_points.bear_case: OpenAI cut its round by a third and 11% on price, Anthropic may land a high-junk rating, and Goldman credit strategists expect BBs to absorb the brunt of AI financing. Investors will lend to hyperscalers but are pickier about the labs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A strong Anthropic IPO pricing in November and an AI stock bounce into year-end would support the bull case. A weaker Anthropic debut would set a lower price for OpenAI's next round.

theme_stances.key_argument: OpenAI cut its round by $10B and its valuation by 11% as the AI selloff and the Anthropic IPO drew investor attention away.
